solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Italian smoker regularly seen in Estonia

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Estonia, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A cigarette-puffing Italian is spotted from time to time in Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian smoker' sounds like a person with a cigarette; it is the Sicilian volcano, which smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily that constantly emits smoke, so it is jokingly an Italian smoker.

clue.text: Majority welcome editor on return, self-effacing

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the majority of something is most of it

indicators.note: on return means the abbreviation for editor is read backwards

explanation.surface: Most people greet a returning editor, who is shy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person plays down their own achievements, which is what self-effacing describes.

clue.text: US politician, comrade, somehow ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the rearranged letters before the abbreviation for time
somehow says the letters of comrade are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: An American politician, a comrade of sorts, arrives early.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two main political parties in the United States.

clue.text: Move quickly as type of jazz brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz

explanation.surface: Someone hurries along while being raised on a certain kind of jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD is British shorthand for traditional (Dixieland-style) jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to make a sudden swift movement, like an arrow flying.

clue.text: Fugitive smuggler

definitions.meaning: a ... is someone who has fled, as in 'do a ...'
a ... also carries contraband, as in a gunrunner or drug ...

explanation.surface: A smuggler on the run from the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Runner covers both a person escaping capture and a person who carries illegal goods across borders.

clue.text: Upset later by a disloyal act

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is upset afterwards by a friend's treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the breaking of trust or faith, the very definition of disloyalty in action.

clue.text: Street loves extremely game fall guy

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O, so two loves give two Os

indicators.note: extremely means taking the letters at the two extremes, first and last, of game

explanation.surface: A street that adores a hugely sporting scapegoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is someone set up to take the blame or be made a fool of, like a fall guy.

clue.text: Wisdom of a copper, soldiers

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
soldiers are often called men in crosswords

explanation.surface: The good sense shown by a police officer and some troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharp insight or shrewd judgement, a close synonym of practical wisdom.

clue.text: A soccer official briefly in Wellington? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for the boot

parts.note: a Wellington is a rubber boot, a welly
ref is the short form of referee, the soccer official

explanation.surface: A referee in wellies? No, quite the reverse: they wear nothing on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay puts A REF in BOOT; then 'Quite the opposite!' says the answer is the reverse of being in a Wellington boot, which is having no shoes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being barefoot means wearing no footwear, the reverse of having your feet in Wellington boots.

clue.text: Emperor's refusal to receive queen

indicators.note: to receive means the word of refusal takes in the other piece

parts.note: no is a refusal
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: An emperor declines to grant an audience to the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor of the first century AD, famed for fiddling while Rome burned.

clue.text: Minister's history uncovered more?

parts.note: history is the past

indicators.note: uncovered means the word more loses its covering letters at each end

explanation.surface: A clergyman's past life has been exposed further.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a Christian minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Desire to show Apple title learners missed?

indicators.note: missed means the learner letters are left out of Apple title

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, so two learners give two Ls

explanation.surface: A craving to show off a title from the tech company Apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Ls from APPLETITLE to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a natural craving or strong wish for something, so it can mean desire.

clue.text: Role key ultimately, for Labour?

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word key

explanation.surface: A key role, in the end, for the workforce?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like work; it is the British Labour Party, an example of a party, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is one of Britain's main political parties, so it is an example of a party.

clue.text: Support deal, step for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of deal and step are rearranged

explanation.surface: Back a deal and step up to make a difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or column on which a statue or vase stands, so it supports it.

clue.text: Copy extract from paper

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters lifted out of the word paper

explanation.surface: Reproduce a passage taken from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them, as apes were thought to do.

clue.text: Length of hair, mine, captivating the French

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A lock of hair enchants a French woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is a length of hair braided from three or more interwoven strands.

clue.text: Part I'm playing, hollow?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of part and I'm are moved about freely

explanation.surface: An actor feels his role is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the arm where it joins the shoulder.

clue.text: Welfare payment, including Channel Islands, easy to manage

indicators.note: including means the payment word takes the abbreviation into itself

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A benefit payment that covers Jersey and Guernsey is no trouble to run.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British islands off Normandy, such as Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile person or animal is meek and compliant, so they are easily controlled.

clue.text: Colour used by officer is excellent

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shade that a top-notch officer adopts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry-red shade, so it is a kind of colour.

clue.text: Check part of tobacco pipe

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to check or halt it
the thin tube of a pipe that runs to the mouthpiece

explanation.surface: Stop the smoker's pipe at one bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem means both to stop or restrain something and the slender shaft of a pipe.

clue.text: Limit referring to first of pair of states — Rhode Island and Connecticut

parts.note: re means about or referring to, as in business letters

indicators.note: first of pair of means the first two letters of the word states, a pair taken from its front

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: A boundary relating to two neighbouring US states in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of pair of states' gives ST, the opening pair of letters of states.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something is to confine it within bounds, which is to limit it.

clue.text: Start to recognise fish and equipment used to catch them?

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word recognise

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Learn to identify fish and the gear an angler uses to land them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points back to fish: a reel is part of a fishing rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is the spool on a fishing rod that winds in the line, gear for catching fish.

clue.text: Was concerned, missing English diamond maybe

indicators.note: missing means the letter for English is left out

parts.note: cared means was concerned

explanation.surface: An English diamond went missing, and someone was worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamond' suggests a gem; it is a playing card of the diamonds suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is one of the four suits, so a diamond can be a playing card.

clue.text: Retracting scandalous information in southeast — big step forward

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word inside the compass abbreviation
retracting means drawing back, so the word for scandal is read backwards

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: A journalist withdraws gossip about southeast England, a major advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retracting' turns the scandal word round, and 'in' sets that inside the compass abbreviation; 'big step forward' reads as progress but is the literal long pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long decisive step, and figuratively a significant advance.

clue.text: Maintain right to invest in something of value

indicators.note: to invest in means to put money into, so the letter for right goes inside

parts.note: an asset is something of value

explanation.surface: Keep the right to put money into a valuable holding.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to insist that it is true, which is to assert it.
